name: MSBuild hygiene
description: Review and tidy .NET project and build files: SDK-style projects, no hard-coded paths, incremental custom targets, analyzers and build-only packages kept private, and conditions that work on every platform. Use when reviewing or changing .csproj, .props or .targets files.
content:
# MSBuild hygiene

Project files are code: keep them short, declarative and the same on every machine.

## Look for

- **Hard-coded paths.** Absolute paths, `..\..\` chains or `C:\`. Use `$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)`, `$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)`, `$(RepoRoot)` (set once in `Directory.Build.props`) and forward slashes, which work everywhere.
- **Old-style leftovers** in SDK-style projects: explicit `<Compile Include>` lists that the default globs already cover (duplicate-item errors), `<Reference HintPath>` to DLLs instead of `PackageReference`/`ProjectReference`, `ToolsVersion`, `packages.config`.
- **Repeated settings.** The same `TargetFramework`, `Nullable`, `LangVersion`, `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, analyzers or package versions in every project. Move them up (see `shared-build-config`).
- **Leaky packages.** Analyzers, source generators and build-only tools without `PrivateAssets="all"`, so they flow to every consumer.
- **Custom targets that always run.** A target that generates or copies files needs `Inputs` and `Outputs` so incremental builds skip it; files it creates must be added to `FileWrites` so `clean` removes them. Prefer `<Copy>` and other built-in tasks over `<Exec>` with shell commands, which break across platforms.
- **Fragile conditions.** `Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'"` is fine; conditions on OS-specific paths or environment variables that aren't set in CI are not. Quote both sides of a comparison.
- **Properties in the wrong file.** Properties that other properties depend on go in `.props` (read before the project); targets, and properties that depend on the SDK's values, go in `.targets` (read after).
- **Warnings switched off wholesale.** `NoWarn` lists that hide real problems. Each suppression needs a reason in a comment, scoped as narrowly as possible.

## How to report and change

- In a review, rank findings by impact (broken or nondeterministic builds first, then slow builds, then tidiness) with the file, line and suggested fix.
- When changing files, build before and after with 0 warnings and make sure the outputs didn't change (same assemblies, same package versions). Use a binary log to compare when unsure (see `msbuild-binlog`).
